Condition: Weight Loss Management for an Obese Person
Textual Review:
I started Zepbound around October 2025, and it’s definitely been an experience. I am 5.7 and before starting I weighed 104kg, which placed me in the obese category. I was also pre-diabetic and had sleep apnea.
Since starting the medication, I’ve lost about 10.2 kg, which I’m genuinely happy about. The weight loss benefits are real and very motivating.
That said, the journey hasn’t been entirely smooth. I’ve experienced palpitations and increased anxiety, and I’ve noticed that these feelings tend to intensify as the dosage increases. At times, it feels like a heightened sense of danger or unease, which has been challenging.
I’m currently weighing the benefits against the side effects. My goal is to reach the 80–89 kg range, at which point I plan to stop and focus on maintaining my weight through lifestyle changes.
Overall, Zepbound works, but the experience will differ for everyone. For me, it’s been effective, though not without its challenges.

Condition: Weight Loss Management for an Obese Person
Textual Review: Everything was ok while I was taking the 0.5 dose in April 2025, but once I began the 7.5 mg. dose on June 19th, I began to notice my blood pressure increasing, and by 9:48 a.m. on the very next day after taking this dose, my BP reading was 155/101 mm Hg with a pulse of 101.  I had to call an ambulance and get to the ER. I don't think Zepbound is for people who already have high blood pressure especially since it raises your heart rate.  I already had diarrhea, and I had no appetite.  Not replacing electrolytes fast enough, my blood sugar had dropped dangerously low.  I was given hydraLazine to bring my BP down quickly, 2 Tylenol, and Ativan to stabilize me before I had a stroke or heart attack.  Everybody is different, so I urge you to really think about all of the pros and cons before taking Zepbound, even if you already have sleep apnea, which I have. I will be looking for alternative ways to lose the 23 pounds, and continue my exercise routine along with the DASH and Mediterranean meal plans.

Textual Review:
When blood work came back during my annual physical earlier this year (2024), my steadily increasing A1C levels had finally crossed over into pre-diabetic. My cholesterol was increasing as well. My blood pressure averaged 145/93, and I was on two medications for that.

My doctor asked if I had thought about the new weight loss drugs Zepbound and Wegovy. He said that both drugs had just received FDA approval for weight loss, that both drugs were remarked/dosed versions of existing drugs to treat diabetes, and that likely insurance would fight to cover them. He suggested Zepbound as he felt it was the better medication, and sure enough, insurance denied it. I got the cash discount from the manufacturer and had two months in savings I could spare, so I paid for the first two months out of pocket. I have never had any side effects to speak of. This was a life-changing medication. I can't state that in any other way. 

After the first month, I had lost almost 20 pounds. My cravings were no longer an issue (and they still aren't). After the second month, I lost another 20 pounds. I could return to the gym and exercise - my body no longer hurt just moving around. My doctor took me off one of my blood pressure meds as my typical blood pressure was now at 108/63. Even my plague psoriasis cleared up (this is NOT a known condition Zepbound treats, but after ten years with psoriasis, it's gone). My insurance finally covered Wegovy, which I have been on since, with a total weight loss now of 56 pounds. My A1C level is back to normal, my blood pressure continues to stabilize in the 116/69 zone, I'm off my psoriasis medication and one of my blood pressure meds. My cholesterol is back to normal. I am eating significantly better than I have in decades. I am consistently working out. Again, this medication is a life changer.
